description:

Scope:
- Verify production hosting/runtime configuration for the web app
- Ensure required environment variables and secrets are present in production
- Deploy current stable build to production
- Validate core site functionality in production (homepage and key flows)
- Document exact URL and deployment status needed for Riot key application

Done criteria:
- Production URL is live and accessible
- Deployment process for urgent updates is confirmed
- We have the information needed to proceed with Riot prod key request

2026-04-18: Landing + legal pages ready to ship. Build verified (`bun run build` produces .svelte-kit/cloudflare/). Next step requires interactive wrangler login by user.

title: Vectorize Plan B event-token recurrence without changing semantics
description: Why: after the WEN/NSZ/4A8 data-path fixes, the canonical-alignment preflight still rejects the retrain at step≈1.36s / epoch≈72m. A representative profile still shows _advance_event_window as the dominant forward hotspot, and the canonical spec requires event-token recurrence but does not require a Python GRUCell loop. What: replace the per-window Python step loop with a more vectorized packed/scan implementation that preserves true event order and between-anchor recurrence semantics. Acceptance: targeted model/train tests still pass, preflight step time drops materially on the current canonical diagnostic, and the implementation remains faithful to event-token recurrence in the canonical spec.
notes: Implemented ordered event-window scan in RSSMCore via batched nn.GRU + packed sequences, and routed Plan B event windows through the scan path. Added regression coverage showing scan-based _advance_event_window matches explicit stepwise recurrence under variable masks. Focused tests passed and canonical preflight now lands at step≈0.65s / epoch≈34.6m (down from ~1.36s / ~72m before this optimization wave).

title: Reduce Plan B per-step static-conditioning overhead while keeping per-step access
description: Why: profiling after the DB optimizations still shows _static_context as a significant hotspot. The canonical spec locks per-step access to static context but leaves the exact conditioning mechanism/open question unsettled downstream, so there is room to make the conditioner cheaper without regressing to seed-only conditioning. What: make event/anchor-step static conditioning materially cheaper (for example via a lighter equivalent per-step conditioner or more aggressive cached projections) while preserving canonical per-step access semantics. Acceptance: targeted model/train tests still pass, preflight step time drops materially on the current canonical diagnostic, and the resulting path is still documented as compliant with the canonical static-stream contract.
notes: Reduced per-step static-conditioning overhead by splitting anchor vs event static queries, batching event-step static attention across the full window, and keeping canonical per-step static access without regressing to seed-only conditioning. Focused tests passed and the updated canonical preflight now clears the runtime gate: step≈0.65s, epoch≈34.6m, earlystop≈4.0h.

title: Stop training-time raw timeline decompression for static match metadata
description: Why: uncached sample loading currently calls get_raw_match() twice per match, and that helper always decompresses both match_json and timeline_json even when the loader only needs champion picks, queue/platform, and participant puuids. Evidence from the audit: decompressing match+timeline averaged about 8.3 ms per sampled match versus about 0.6 ms for match_json alone. What: normalize or cache the needed static metadata so training paths no longer have to decompress timeline blobs. Acceptance: the sample loader no longer pays full timeline decompression for static/player metadata access, and measured per-sample raw DB overhead drops materially.
notes: Stopped training paths from inflating timeline blobs when only match metadata is needed. Added get_raw_match_only() and threaded preloaded match dict through static feature building. On 200 real matches: raw match+timeline decode 8.11ms mean vs match-only 1.04ms mean.

title: Narrow and index Plan B event queries by match/timestamp
description: Why: event-table access is the biggest remaining database-side cost in sample loading. Evidence from the audit: tokenizer and macro-feature queries both hit the 67.2M-row events table, both sort with a temp B-tree, and the macro path loads about 4.8k events per sampled match while only needing about 317 objective events. What: add the right match/timestamp indexes and change dataset/tokenizer event queries to pull only the event subsets they actually need. Acceptance: EXPLAIN no longer shows temp ORDER BY sorts on the hot match-scoped event queries, and representative timings improve materially.
notes: Implemented filtered event queries + match/timestamp index coverage. Added query-plan test asserting no temp B-tree sort on hot tokenizer/macro event queries. On 200 real matches: tokenizer query 5.40ms -> 1.50ms mean, macro objective query 1.32ms -> 0.39ms mean.

title: Audit training databases for remaining performance bottlenecks
description: Why: the canonical retrain preflight still projects an overlong run, so we need another pass over the SQLite-backed training databases and the queries they serve to find remaining bottlenecks. What: inspect the live schemas, table sizes, indexes, and the code paths that hit them; identify high-leverage database improvements; and document concrete next steps. Acceptance: a ranked list of database-side improvement opportunities is produced with evidence from schema/query inspection, and any follow-up implementation work is filed as beads if needed.
notes: Findings: (1) event-table scans are the dominant DB-side sample-load cost; EXPLAIN shows temp ORDER BY B-trees on match-scoped event queries, and the macro path loads ~4.8k events/match while only needing ~317 objective events. (2) raw_matches access is overpaying for timeline decompression; match+timeline averaged ~8.3 ms vs ~0.6 ms for match_json only, and the loader currently calls get_raw_match() twice. (3) player feature preload/index build still spend startup time on DISTINCT/GROUP BY over frames; full-train build_puuid_index took ~11.0 s and MatchDataset init took ~22.8 s. Follow-up beads: wen, nsz, 4a8.

title: Add Plan B pre-training optimization preflight hook
description: Why: full canonical training runs are expensive enough that we should refuse or at least loudly gate runs when the current model/training surface is obviously suboptimal. What: add a pre-training hook that runs a short optimization preflight before full plan-b training, checks for key efficiency/optimality signals, and stops or warns before launching the long run if thresholds are not met. Acceptance: full plan-b-train invokes the preflight automatically before the long run; the hook reports its checks and estimated risk; and there is a test covering the preflight path.
notes: Added automatic pre-training preflight to plan_b_train with efficiency + projected-runtime gates and test coverage. The current canonical diagnostic now prints token/anchor/recur efficiency plus projected epoch/early-stop time and correctly rejects runs that would waste hours (currently step≈1.36s, epoch≈72.0m, earlystop≈8.4h).

title: Remove host-sync hotspots from Plan B event-window recurrence
description: Why: the canonical model forward path performs many Python-side .item()/.any()-driven loops while gathering and advancing event windows, which likely forces frequent host synchronization on GPU. What: rework the recurrent event-window path to avoid per-sample scalar syncs and reduce Python overhead in forward/rollout code. Acceptance: the hottest recurrence path no longer depends on repeated tensor-to-Python scalar extraction in the steady-state forward; tests cover the new behavior; retrain bead 9b01bf83-51r depends on this work.
notes: Vectorized event-window gather and removed the repeated .any() gate from steady-state recurrence. Added regression coverage for variable-count windows. Representative profiling still points to event recurrence as the next hotspot, but the steady-state forward path no longer performs the old per-sample scalar-sync pattern.

title: Bucket Plan B training batches by sequence/event cost
description: Why: the canonical retrain now mixes very short and very long games in the same batch, wasting a large fraction of token/event recurrence compute on padding and masked windows. What: add a length-aware batching path for plan-b-train so batches group similar-cost games together, and preserve shuffle across buckets per epoch. Acceptance: training code uses a bucketed sampler or equivalent cost-aware batching; representative diagnostics show improved batch efficiency vs random mixing; retrain bead 9b01bf83-51r depends on this work.
notes: Implemented BucketedBatchSampler + DB-backed sort keys in plan_b_train. Preflight now reports token_eff=0.939, anchor_eff=0.922, recur_eff=0.720 on the canonical diagnostic instead of the much lower mixed-batch efficiency seen in the audit.

title: Rerun M4 retrieval check on canonical-alignment checkpoint
description: Why: the current retrieval report is attached to the pre-overhaul model. After the aligned checkpoint lands, retrieval and its interpretation need to be recomputed on the new representation. What: rebuild the retrieval index on the aligned checkpoint, rerun the entropy gate and baseline contrast on both holdouts, and refresh the per-minute tables used by downstream M4 follow-ups. Acceptance: an updated retrieval report exists for the aligned checkpoint; the index artifact metadata references the new checkpoint/code sha; and downstream M4 diagnostic beads can depend on this rerun instead of the older proxy-era report.

title: Train and evaluate first canonical-alignment world-model checkpoint
description: Why: once the canonical architecture deltas land, the project needs an explicit retrain/eval pass rather than treating retraining as implicit cleanup. What: train a new checkpoint on the current corpus after the canonical-overhaul beads land, then rerun the Plan B-style evaluation suite with game-cold, player-cold, leak-probe, and rollout diagnostics. Acceptance: a new checkpoint and eval report are produced; the report names the canonical inputs/targets used; and any remaining proxy caveats are called out explicitly.

title: Align decoder heads on [h_t || z_t] anchor representation
description: Why: the canonical spec defines r_t = [h_t || z_t] as the shared anchor representation for prediction, while the current implementation still drives decoder heads mostly from z_t alone. What: move the four core decoder heads onto the shared [h_t || z_t] representation and keep retrieval on [h_t || mu_q(z_t)] so training and downstream retrieval finally agree on the anchor contract. Acceptance: next-event, next-observation, outcome, and next-decision heads all consume the shared anchor representation; tests and checkpoints reflect the new dimensional contract.
notes:
Files: code/model/plan_b_model.py — all four decoder heads (next_event_head, next_obs_head, outcome_head, next_decision_head) currently read z_t (dim D_Z=32). Move them to r_t = cat(h_t, z_t) (dim D_H+D_Z = 544). Retrieval key stays [h_t || mu_q(z_t)] — no retrieval change needed.

Dimensional change: head input Linear layers go from in_features=32 to in_features=544. Update all affected head MLP input dims and corresponding test fixtures.

Lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires.
Aligned all four decoder heads on the shared anchor representation r_t = [h_t || z_t]. Added explicit anchor_repr output plus a shared decode_anchor_repr() path so teacher-forced decoding, rollout decoding, and retrieval all agree on the anchor contract.
close_reason: Decoder heads now consume shared [h_t || z_t] anchor representations

title: Replace pooled between-anchor summaries with event-token recurrence
description: Why: the canonical spec locks hybrid time and requires event tokens to update the world model between anchors. The current pooled per-minute action_summary remains a temporary proxy. What: advance the recurrent state in true event order within each anchor interval, then apply the anchor posterior update at the observation boundary. Acceptance: event tokens are no longer collapsed to one mean-pooled summary per anchor window; recurrence runs over ordered event tokens; batching/tests cover variable event counts and anchor boundaries.
notes:
Files: code/model/plan_b_model.py (RSSM forward — replace mean-pool of action_summary with per-event GRU steps between anchor boundaries), code/model/dataset.py (preserve event token order within each anchor window; pass event timestamps for ordering), code/model/encoders.py (event token embedding must carry subtype/payload from kzx before this bead lands).

The pooled action_summary is a temporary proxy that the canonical spec explicitly calls out. Event tokens must advance recurrent state in true time order.

Batching constraint: variable event counts per anchor window — use packed sequences or masking, not padding to a fixed max.

Lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires.
Replaced pooled action-summary recurrence with true ordered event-token recurrence. MatchDataset now batches event windows as flat position streams plus per-window counts/offsets (no fixed 128-token padding), PlanBModel advances h over each event in true order between anchors, and anchor batching now tracks anchor_mask so mixed-length batches do not train on padded anchors.
close_reason: Implemented true event-token recurrence between anchors

title: Condition static game context at every model step
description: Why: the canonical world-model spec requires Stream 1 to condition the sequence model at every anchor/event step, not just seed h0. Today Plan B uses static_to_h(static) to initialize the recurrent state and then mostly drops static context. What: represent static game context as per-game tokens (champion/side tokens plus a misc-context token for queue, region, time bucket, patch params, etc.) and add a per-step conditioning path so dynamic updates can attend to static context throughout the sequence. Acceptance: static context is available to every dynamic update step; the implementation no longer treats h0 seeding alone as compliant Stream-1 conditioning; tests cover shape/plumbing and preserve leak discipline.
notes:
Files: code/model/plan_b_model.py (RSSM forward — add cross-attention layer at each anchor/event step), code/model/encoders.py (StaticEncoder output → token set, not scalar), code/model/dataset.py (static tokens through to model if shape changes).

Cross-attention is required per spec — FiLM/gating or h0-seed-only does not satisfy the per-step access requirement. static_to_h() is explicitly non-compliant after this bead lands.

Lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires. Must not be merged independently as a partial change.
Implemented per-step static conditioning with tokenized static context, cross-attention at each RSSM step, and coverage in encoder/model tests. Landed together with 3h8/3iv/kzx in the same implementation batch as required by the spec notes.
close_reason: Implemented tokenized static context with per-step cross-attention

title: Plan first architecture-alignment retrain from canonical world-model spec
description: Why: the new canonical world-model spec names a set of open questions that must be answered deliberately before the next model-alignment retrain. What: produce an implementation/retraining plan that decides the first full-fidelity anchor observation bundle, the event target factorization, the static conditioning mechanism, the recurrence staging strategy, and whether head inputs move to [h||z] in the same retrain. Acceptance: the follow-up plan references the canonical spec, records decisions for those five questions, and sequences the existing implementation beads so the next retrain scope is explicit.
notes: Delivered docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md, created the missing canonical-alignment beads, and rewired dependencies so the implementation queue now phases through inputs -> recurrence/heads -> rollout -> retrain -> retrieval.

title: Write canonical superpowers model spec
description: Why: the original sequence-model spec captures the strict long-term goals, but downstream Plan A / Plan B / M4 docs introduced milestone proxies and partial gates that are now distributed across several files. What: add a new canonical spec under docs/superpowers/specs that preserves the original draft, reconciles the downstream docs, clearly separates source-of-truth architecture from milestone approximations, and records the open questions raised by the stricter design. Acceptance: a new spec file exists; it does not overwrite the 2026-04-15 sequence-model spec; it explains final architecture vs temporary proxies vs open questions; it is specific enough to guide later code changes and retraining decisions.

title: Expand anchor observations with richer timeline and team-macro features
description:
Plan doc decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md §1 — first full-fidelity anchor observation bundle.

**Why:** AnchorObservationProjector sees 10×6 features (total_gold, xp, level, pos_x, pos_y, cs). Canonical spec requires rich participant + team/objective state for a fair test of the architecture.

**What — per-participant features (10 participants):**
- total_gold, current_gold, xp, level, cs, jungle_cs
- kills, deaths, assists
- pos_x, pos_y
- frame-native health/power summaries if cleanly available from parser frames

**What — team/objective macro features:**
- gold_diff, xp_diff, kill_diff (blue minus red)
- tower_diff, plate_diff
- neutral objective counts/state: drake count + type, grubs, Herald, Baron, Elder (present/taken)
- team centroid/spread if already derivable without new parser work

**Files:** code/model/dataset.py (frame feature extraction in MatchDataset._build_anchor_obs or equivalent), code/model/encoders.py (AnchorObservationProjector — expand 10×6 input), code/features.py (reuse existing macro feature helpers where possible)

**Scope cut:** do NOT block on reconstructing a per-frame full inventory vector. Inventory/warding summaries are allowed only where trivially derivable from existing parser output. Full item-state fidelity belongs in the event stream (kzx).

**Acceptance:**
- AnchorObservationProjector input dim > 60 (was 60)
- current_gold, jungle_cs, kills/deaths/assists present per participant
- At least gold_diff and tower_diff present as team macro features
- Neutral objective state (drake count, baron present) present
- All features sourced from frame data stored by parser — no future data
- Existing tests pass; new tests cover per-participant and macro feature shapes
- This bead lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires
notes: Expanded anchor observations beyond 10x6: per-participant current_gold, jungle_cs, kills/deaths/assists, positions, plus team/objective macro features (gold/xp/kill/tower/plate/objective diffs and centroid/spread) now feed the observation projector.

title: Make world-model tokens target-aware and subtype-aware
description:
Plan doc decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md §2 — factorized next-event objective, not a single flat categorical.

**Why:** tokenizer.py emits target_slot but dataset/model drops it. events.details fields (itemId, skillSlot, monsterType, laneType, towerType, buildingType) are ignored. The model cannot distinguish boots from IE, Q from R, or tower types. This breaks both teaching and counterfactual reasoning.

**What — token schema extension:**
- Surface target_slot through dataset into the model (already parsed, just dropped)
- Per-event-type payload fields:
  - ITEM_PURCHASED → item_id (integer, embed separately)
  - SKILL_LEVEL_UP → skill_slot (0–3 for Q/W/E/R)
  - ELITE_MONSTER_KILL → monster_subtype (drake type, grub, herald, baron, elder)
  - BUILDING_KILL → building_type × lane_type × tower_type
  - WARD_PLACED / WARD_KILL → ward_subtype (control, yellow, blue totem)

**What — head factorization:**
- Replace flat next-event categorical head with factorized heads:
  - coarse event type head
  - actor slot head
  - target slot head (where applicable)
  - per-type subtype/payload head, gated/masked by event type
- Factorization keeps class counts manageable without losing semantic richness

**Files:** code/model/tokenizer.py (surface payload fields), code/model/dataset.py (pass target_slot + payloads through collation), code/model/encoders.py (token embedding for target + subtypes), code/model/plan_b_model.py (replace flat event head with factorized heads), affected tests

**Acceptance:**
- ITEM_PURCHASED token carries item_id embedding
- SKILL_LEVEL_UP token carries skill_slot (Q/W/E/R distinguishable)
- Event head loss is factorized — no single flat event-type-only categorical
- target_slot flows through dataset and is embedded in the model
- Tests cover token schema shapes and factorized head output dims
- This bead lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires
notes: Surfaced target_slot and event payload fields through tokenizer/dataset/encoders, and replaced the flat next-event head with a factorized event head (type + actor + target + gated payload heads).

title: Fill out static game-context stream beyond patch version scaffolding
description:
Plan doc decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md §3 — adopt tokenized static context with per-step cross-attention. This bead delivers the feature bundle; c1m wires the per-step conditioning path.

**Why:** static_to_h() seeds h0 with a 3-dim patch-version triple and drops all other game-start context. Canonical spec requires champion picks, side assignments, queue, region, time-of-day, and patch params as first-class static inputs.

**What:**
- Replace or extend patch_vector_for_match() to produce a full static feature bundle:
  - 10 champion IDs (one per participant slot, embedded separately in the encoder)
  - blue/red side per participant (10 binary flags)
  - queue ID (categorical)
  - region (categorical)
  - time-of-day bucket (categorical or scalar)
  - patch version triple (keep existing, richer numeric params deferred)
- Update StaticEncoder / static_to_h path in code/model/encoders.py to consume the new schema
- Leak discipline: all features must be game-start only — no frame, event, or outcome data

**Files:** code/model/dataset.py (static feature extraction), code/model/encoders.py (StaticEncoder), code/model/plan_b_model.py (forward signature if static shape changes), affected tests

**Scope cut:** rich numeric patch params (item/champ/monster stats from Data Dragon) are deferred to a later pass. Do not block this bead on Data Dragon ingestion.

**Acceptance:**
- Static vector has substantially more than 3 non-zero dims
- Champion pick IDs are present per participant slot
- Side/queue/region/time-of-day features are present
- No frame, event, or outcome data in the static bundle
- All existing tests pass; new tests cover schema shape and leak invariant
- This bead lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires
notes: Implemented the canonical static feature bundle via model/static_features.py and StaticContextEncoder updates: champion picks, sides, queue, region, time bucket, and patch vector now flow through the dataset/model path without using future information.

title: Grow corpus to 50k games for prod-scale training
description:
Scale the match DB from current size to 50k games for production training runs.

Why: Current dataset is fast for iteration but undersized for prod-quality model. 50k is the first prod milestone.

What needs to be done:
- Keep current small dataset intact as fast-test fixture (used by 4tl and model-specific tests)
- Collect/fetch 50k games into a separate prod corpus DB
- Audit all pipeline stages (preprocessing, indexing, RSSM training, retrieval) for robustness at 50k scale — memory usage, wall-clock time, file sizes
- Explore compression options (zstd, sqlite VACUUM, columnar formats) and/or alternative storage (HF bucket, DuckDB on disk)
- Document storage decision: where prod corpus lives, how it's versioned, how to handoff to GPU host
- Update 4tl (exclude_match_id) and other components to work with both small and large corpus

Constraints:
- Git repo must not contain the corpus DB — store externally (HF bucket preferred)
- GPU host workflow: corpus must be copyable cleanly per existing handoff procedure

title: Lift train-set self-retrieval: add exclude_match_id to query_index
description:
Today `generate_lesson` refuses to process train-set matches because the M4 retrieval index was built from train games; querying from a train match returns itself as its own top-k neighbour and collapses the cohort.

Fix: parameter-level filter, no index rebuild.

**Changes:**
- `code/model/retrieval.py::query_index` — accept optional `exclude_match_ids: set[str] | None`. Fetch top-`k + buffer` with `buffer = len(exclude) + small_margin`, mask cohort rows whose `bundle.row_match_id` ∈ exclude, trim back to `k`. Default None = current behavior.
- `code/model/lesson.py::generate_lesson` — always pass `exclude_match_ids={match_id}`. Drop the "holdout only" caveat from module docstring.
- `code/tests/model/test_lesson.py` — integration test on a train-set match_id (pick first from plan_a_holdout minus … actually just any `load_split('train')[0]`) asserting cohort doesn't contain target.

**Why not rebuild:** the 800 MB index is checkpoint-bound. Masking is O(k·|exclude|) per query, trivial.

**Acceptance:**
- lesson CLI runs on a train-set match_id and returns cohorts that do not contain the target match_id.
- All existing tests pass.

title: M5-MVP: inference-path lesson CLI
description:
Wire existing Plan B checkpoint + M4 retrieval index into an end-to-end inference CLI that produces per-game lesson-anchor candidates.

**Why:** 12.8k-game train + M4 gate passed; the learning side of the pipeline is complete but nothing consumes the artifacts yet. The inference path needs at least a minimal lesson surface so we can validate end-to-end signal before building the full M5 teaching UI.

**Scope (MVP):**
- New `code/model/lesson.py` with `generate_lesson(match_id, team='blue', k=64)` that:
  - loads `plan_b_full_best.pt` + `plan_b_index.pt`
  - encodes the target game's anchors
  - queries the index per mid-game anchor (10..25)
  - returns per-anchor cohort entropy + cohort winrate + cohort match_ids
  - picks best mistake-anchor (player lost, max entropy) and strength-anchor (player won, max entropy)
- `model.cli lesson --match-id X [--team blue|red] [--k 64]` subcommand emitting JSON
- Smoke test: generate a lesson for the first game in `plan_a_holdout.txt` and assert structure

**Out of scope:**
- Actual "what separated the cohorts" content (decision/event decoder) — next slice
- Site wiring / DB schema changes
- FAISS swap (deferred beads-l2z)

**Acceptance:**
- `uv run python -m model.cli lesson --match-id <holdout_id>` returns valid JSON
- Smoke test passes
close_reason: MVP landed: lesson CLI + tests + end-to-end smoke pass on real holdout game

title: M4 retrieval check: kNN over Plan B latent + entropy gate
description:
Build the kNN retrieval layer over the Plan B [h_t || mu_q(z_t)] latent
and verify mean cohort outcome entropy >= 0.7 bits at k=64 on both
holdouts (game-cold, player-cold), restricted to mid-game anchors
(minutes 10-25).

## Spec
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-17-m4-retrieval-check-design.md

## Plan
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-m4-retrieval-check.md (16 tasks)

## Gate (both holdouts must pass)
- mean cohort outcome entropy >= 0.7 bits at k=64
- model k=64 entropy < random-k entropy (should be ~1.0)
- model k=64 entropy <= static-only and frame-features baselines

## Deliverables
- code/model/retrieval.py, code/model/m4_eval.py
- code/model/baselines/{static_only,frame_features}_index.py
- data/retrieval/plan_b_*_index.pt (gitignored, HF-uploaded)
- docs/m4_retrieval_eval_report_<date>.md

## Follow-ups (already filed)
- howtowin.lol-l2z: FAISS backend
- howtowin.lol-cow: h_t-only / z_t-only ablations
- howtowin.lol-rzz: player-only baseline
notes:
Session 2026-04-17: T0-T14 complete, pushed to origin/core through 2c282f4.

Code: retrieval.py, m4_eval.py, baselines/{static_only,frame_features}_index.py, CLI subcommands retrieval-build / retrieval-eval. 109 model-dir tests pass.

Local smoke (T14): ckpt=plan_b_smoke_best.pt, 50-game corpus, 1325 rows built; 64-query eval round-trip OK (k=8 entropy 0.294 — not meaningful, smoke ckpt was max_puuids=50, not the gate run).

REMAINING: T15 runbook on GPU host — build all three indexes + eval + report + verify gate + commit report + close this epic. Requires the real plan_b_full_best.pt checkpoint on the GPU. Session hand-off point.

description: The docs/superpowers model draft has drifted in a few important ways that make the current story internally inconsistent. Follow-up should tighten the documentation, not necessarily change code. Issues found during the 2026-04-22 review: (1) core sequence spec says static stream includes picks/sides/queue/region/time-of-day and is cross-attended each anchor, but Plan A/Plan B plans/self-reviews treat patch_params + StaticContextEncoder as covering that scope; (2) core spec says next-event head is categorical over event type × actor × target and event tokens feed RSSM between anchors, but Plan B design/plan quietly relax this to multi-hot 11-class event windows and pooled action summaries; (3) Plan B design says KL weight starts at 0.01 and static encoder is 1024→512→512 cross-attended each step, while the implementation plan uses D_STATIC=512 despite reusing Plan A encoders and maps the KL setting to KL_WEIGHT_LOSS=0.05 with only a hand-wavy equivalence note; (4) M4 retrieval spec uses a one-sided entropy gate (>=0.7) even though the same doc says random cohorts are ~1.0 and bad, so the real success condition is a band/baseline comparison, not a simple threshold; (5) surrounding eval reports should be reconciled with spec gate text where monotonic AUC / rollout ordering were expected but not observed. Deliverable: update the docs so the intended model draft, temporary simplifications, and actual acceptance criteria are explicit and non-contradictory.

title: Design: latent archetypes for lesson-plan personalization (not retrieval)
description:
Scope design pass for archetype work. User constraint: archetypes are **latent, fluid, multi-dimensional** (role, time-of-day, intra-game phase can all shift them) and must NOT be used to filter retrieval cohorts. Cohorts remain action-basis (z_t retrieval). Archetypes feed only the lesson-plan selector — *how* we teach, not *what* we retrieve.

Why this separation:
- Counterfactual signal lives in the state-nearest cohort. Filtering the cohort by archetype throws away the "same situation, different outcome" evidence the whole M4 gate validated.
- Archetype matters for lesson framing + sequencing: a greedy-farm archetype and a greedy-roam archetype may both be "in this state" but the minute-4 advice differs in wording and focus.

Design questions to settle before implementing:
1. **Representation.** Three candidates:
   a. Single continuous embedding per (puuid, session) — lives in latent space, no discrete labels surfaced.
   b. Short-window trajectory fingerprint (last N anchors of h_t) — captures intra-game shifts.
   c. Behaviour-stat vector from crafted features — interpretable, good for "you always X" prose.
   Likely hybrid: (a) for personalization routing, (c) for lesson prose substitutions.
2. **Conditioning signal.** role, time-of-day, game-phase. Is role already in player_features? Add session-clock bucket, anchor-minute bucket for intra-game drift.
3. **Lesson-plan policy.** Given archetype vector and cohort output, how does lesson selection condition on it? Options: (i) fixed prompt templates keyed to nearest-archetype-centroid; (ii) learned policy over (archetype × cohort-split) → lesson variant.
4. **A/B harness.** Lesson variant id → impression → later outcome (KDA delta, winrate on same champ/role in next N games). Where does this storage live? Site analytics DB.
5. **Ethics/UX.** Archetypes stay internal — never shown to user as a label. Avoid "you are a Late-Ganking Jungler" framing; instead surface behaviour ("your first gank averages 5:30 vs cohort 3:45").

Deliverable of this bead: design doc under `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-archetype-lesson-personalization-design.md` with chosen representation, lesson-plan integration, and A/B plan. Implementation plan + tasks follow as separate beads.

**Non-goals:** actual clustering code, any retrieval modification, any UI.

title: M4 follow-up: inverted per-minute entropy curve
description:
In the M4 eval report (docs/m4_retrieval_eval_report_2026-04-17.md) the per-minute mean cohort outcome entropy at k=64 on both holdouts is highest near minute 10 and drops monotonically toward minute 25:

game_cold:   min10=0.817 -> min25=0.623
player_cold: min10=0.858 -> min25=0.600

This is the inverse of the expected "mid-game is most uncertain" shape. Plan self-review flagged this as a follow-up.

Hypotheses to check:
- model has learned late-game is more discriminable than early-game (plausible: more tempo signals accumulated by min 20+, draft-to-outcome mapping tighter)
- cohort construction collapses as h_t trajectories converge late-game (possible if model under-uses z_t)
- minute-bucket quantization rounds away a real mid-game peak

Next steps:
- log per-minute n_queries alongside entropy (sample-size effect?)
- compare h_t-only vs z_t-only vs full-key (see howtowin.lol-cow ablation)
- inspect a handful of anchors per bucket to eyeball cohort quality

title: M4 follow-up: FAISS-backed retrieval index for production inference
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

The M4 eval index is PyTorch native brute force (exact, ~1 GB tensor, batched cdist+topk on GPU). Adequate for offline eval (~2k queries against 450k corpus). Inadequate for any online surface that needs sub-second per-query lookup at scale.

Swap to FAISS (`IndexFlatL2` first; `IndexIVFFlat` if quantization noise is acceptable) once M5 or any user-facing surface needs it. Keep the same `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` whitened-key contract so the artifact is interchangeable.

**Why:** isolates the dependency-add from the gating-eval work. Lets us prove the model is good *before* paying the FAISS-install + index-format cost.

**How to apply:** trigger when M5 lesson-generator design surfaces a per-anchor latency budget that brute force can't meet, or when corpus grows past ~5M anchors.

title: M4 follow-up: h_t-only and z_t-only ablation baselines
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run two more kNN retrieval evals against the same held-out queries:
- index over `h_t` alone (512-dim, whitened)
- index over `mu_q(z_t)` alone (32-dim, whitened)

Compare entropy curves to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** tells us which sub-block of the concatenated latent actually carries the retrieval signal. If `h_t`-only matches the headline, the stochastic latent is decorative for retrieval; if `z_t`-only matches, the GRU history is. Either finding informs M5 (teaching surface) and any future RSSM iteration.

**How to apply:** only run if the headline M4 entropy disappoints (<0.7 bits) or sits suspiciously close to a single sub-block's expected ceiling. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the slice.

title: M4 follow-up: player-only baseline kNN
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run the same kNN retrieval eval but with the index built over the Plan B player-stream encoder output only (10× per-participant features, no static, no dynamic). Compare cohort outcome entropy to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** clarifies whether retrieval signal is dominated by "similar lineups + skill" rather than "similar in-game state." If player-only nearly matches the headline, the dynamic latent is redundant for retrieval purposes (a finding worth knowing).

**How to apply:** only run after the headline M4 result lands and only if cohort coherence is ambiguous. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the encoder.

title: Set up git-LFS workflow for Hugging Face model repo
description:
For cases where hf upload / hf sync isn't enough (e.g., frequent weight iterations where git history on weights is useful), set up direct git+LFS push to a Hugging Face model repo.

Steps:
- Install git-lfs (pacman -S git-lfs on Arch, apt on Debian-likes)
- Decide which checkpoints warrant repo-versioned LFS vs plain hf upload (rule of thumb: LFS when diffable, bucket/upload when archival)
- hf repos create nyx-haile/howtowin-plan-b-rssm-v1 --type model
- git clone the HF repo, git lfs install, git lfs track "*.pt" "*.safetensors"
- Commit .gitattributes and a first weight file, push via https with HF_TOKEN
- Document the workflow in docs/ and add to a project script (scripts/upload_checkpoint.py)

Depends on admin-3wd (credential helper) for the git push step not to leak the HF token to ~/.git-credentials plaintext.
